source.title: Neural Representations Reveal Distinct Modes of Class Fitting in Residual Convolutional Networks

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendix, is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies class-conditional representation density, example memorization and adversarial robustness. It does not measure the training–test generalization gap or test any listed version's specific intervention or measure.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on random-label fitting and memorization but reports no random-label experiment. Its own results concern class representations and their associations with memorization and robustness; these are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study measures class-representation density, memorization, and certified robustness. None of its own experiments tests V1–V8. In particular, excluding density bins and evaluating the excluded examples does not test whether removing highly memorized examples harms independent test accuracy more than random removal, as V8 specifies.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. More precisely, the authors infer compact, spatially separated representation components in high-density classes and report greater memorization than for examples with intermediate class-conditional density, together with lower certified robustness. They interpret this as support for the long-tail account, but do not directly establish V8's removal effect.
record.recipe_differences: Measures class-conditional representation distributions and their associations with memorization and robustness; it does not reproduce the generalization-gap, optimizer, regularization or sharpness comparisons in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, architecture, network stage, and density-bin group are reported as affecting the observed patterns. The two density modes occur in later rather than early stages and were not observed in the plain convolutional comparator.

fits_no_version.finding: Across density bins, average memorization decreases within the low-density regime, then increases abruptly at the transition to high-density classes. Models retrained without each bin are evaluated on its excluded examples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Class-conditional representation density is associated with memorization and performance on excluded density bins in the tested ResNets.

fits_no_version.finding: The transition to high-density classes coincides with lower certified radii and smoothed-classifier F-scores, with slightly more abstention.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: High-density class representations are associated with lower randomized-smoothing robustness in the tested ResNets.

fits_no_version.finding: Later ResNet stages exhibit distinct density modes. High-density classes have greater distributional complexity without smaller mean intra-class distances. The plain convolutional comparator lacks these modes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested residual convolutional networks exhibit stage-dependent class-representation density modes absent from the tested plain convolutional network.

fits_no_version.finding: Class representations form mostly between stages two and three for both memorized and typical examples; memorized examples have slightly less distinct class representations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Memorized and typical examples exhibit similar progression of class separation across ResNet stages.

record.problems: The study does not measure train–test error gaps. Several plotted quantities are described qualitatively without numerical values in the text. Memorization-score estimates exhibit large variance. Mini-ImageNet memorization estimates and modified stride settings differ from the CIFAR-100 setup; ImageNet-scale analyses were omitted for computational cost.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately stated numeric results on the listed versions were reported. Figure-only plotted values without textual numeric descriptions are not transcribed as numeric rows.

untested.parts: No paired random-label and natural-label training and held-out accuracy experiment.
No width sweep measuring test error beyond zero training error.
No convolutional-versus-fully-connected test-error comparison or test of local connectivity.
No dropout intervention and held-out-error comparison.
No magnitude-aware weight sharpness, generalization-gap ranking, or comparison against norm and margin measures.
No comparison of independent test accuracy after removing the most-memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are assessed against the listed versions; cannot_determine does not dispute the reported adjacent findings. Fig. 3 also reports Mini-ImageNet memorization and ordinary excluded-bin F-scores, which R1–R2 omit, but these do not warrant version-linked missing entries. The absence of a training–test gap alone is not grounds for exclusion; the specific interventions and comparisons in V1–V8 are absent.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare fitting random and natural labels or report held-out accuracy for either.
No width sweep or test-error results across widths.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks on image test error.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or training–test gap comparison.
The study excludes density bins from training and evaluates those examples, but does not compare removal of the most-memorized examples with removal of random examples.

rows.subject: ResNet50
rows.operation_detail: Compared class-conditional log-density and memorization across 50 density bins; separately trained models excluding each bin and evaluated F-score on that bin.

conditions.value: 50 equally sized bins, ordered by estimated class-conditional log-density

rows.measure: Mean memorization score and F-score on examples excluded from training
rows.value: Up to the transition between low- and high-density classes, memorization decreases on average with increasing density; it then rises abruptly and remains largely independent of density. F-scores are in close agreement with mean memorization scores.
rows.uncertainty: The text says memorization scores exhibit large variance; no numerical uncertainty stated for these trends.
rows.locator: Results, “Class representations correlate with memorization and adversarial robustness”; Fig. 3
rows.note: The study describes the trend across bins, not a targeted comparison of removing highly memorized examples against random removal.
rows.check: Density-bin memorization and performance on excluded bin examples do not measure V8's targeted-versus-random removal effect on test accuracy.

rows.check: Certified input-perturbation robustness is not V7's magnitude-aware weight sharpness or any other listed outcome.

rows.subject: plain 8-layer convolutional network
rows.operation_detail: Compared class-conditional log-density structure across hidden layers with residual-network results.
rows.measure: Presence of distinct class-fitting modes across layers
rows.value: Classes are fitted uniformly across all hidden layers; distinct modes were not observed.
rows.locator: Appendix, “Distinct modes of class fitting in residual convolutional networks”; Fig. A.8
rows.note: Comparator result about representation structure; it does not test V3's test-error comparison.
rows.check: The absence of density modes in a plain convolutional network does not test V3's convolutional-versus-fully-connected test-error comparison.
